verdict.rationale: Reflect's site describes itself as an open-source, local-first app: code is on GitHub, notes are local Markdown files, you choose your own sync (iCloud Drive or Git), and you can bring your own AI API key. That points to running the core product on your own setup without the vendor's servers. However, other first-party docs describe a vendor-hosted service (an OAuth API at reflect.app, server-side end-to-end encryption, publishing, calendar sync), so it is unclear how much of the product works when self-run. Missing for 10: documented self-hosting or deployment instructions, clarity on which hosted features work without vendor servers, and independent or hands-on corroboration of self-hosting.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: An open-source note-taking app with daily notes, backlinks, and local Markdown files.
